newsitem.title: UK: BT beats rivals in German court challenge - FT.
newsitem.headline: BT beats rivals in German court challenge - FT.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc has claimed victory in a landmark court case in Germany which could have "profound implications for the future of competition in Europe's telecoms markets", the Financial Times said on Friday.

The paper said the Dusseldorf High Court ruled on Thursday that Global One, the strategic alliance between BT rivals Deutsche Telekom AG, France Telecom and Sprint Corp of the U.S., had been in breach of European competition rules.
The complaint by BT and its German partner, VIAG AG, was that Global One had started trading before meeting conditions imposed on it by the European Commission (EC).
The court ruled that Deutsche Telekom was liable for costs and damages, which could amount to "tens of millions of pounds", the paper said, adding that the figure would be determined at a later date.

The paper said the alliance had agreed with the EC to begin trading, providing services to multinational companies, only once two or more licences had been issued to competitors in France and Germany.
"In fact, Global One admitted it began trading several months before meeting the Commission's conditions," the Financial Times said.

"The ruling should go some way towards reassuring investors who are worried that regulation in Europe's liberalising telecoms markets will favour incumbents at the expense of rival operators," the paper said.

"If Global One had been allowed to proceed in breach of the Commission's conditions, it would have gained an illegal advantage at a time when the market is at a critical stage of development," the head of BT's German joint venture, Lutz Meyer-Scheel, was quoted as saying.
